title: An fppf torus splits on an etale cover
statement: Let $S$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $T\to S$ an $S$-group scheme, meaning an object of schemes over $S$ with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group diagrams. Suppose $T$ is a relative torus [def-sfb-relative-torus]: there is an fppf covering family $S_i\to S$ [def-pc-fppf-site] on which $T\times_S S_i\simeq\mathbf G_{m,S_i}^{r_i}$ as group schemes for finite integers $r_i\geq0$. Here $\mathbf G_{m,W}(V)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)^\times$ on $W$-schemes $V$, and rank zero denotes the trivial group. Then there exist a set-indexed family of schemes $U_j$, etale morphisms $U_j\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with jointly covering images, finite-rank free abelian groups $M_j$, and isomorphisms of $U_j$-group schemes $T\times_S U_j\simeq D_{U_j}(M_j)$. Products are [def-pc-fibre-product]; $D_W(M)$ is obtained by gluing the affine diagonalizable groups $D_C(M)=\operatorname{Spec}C[M]$ of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}C\subset W$. No finite, connected, normal, Noetherian or henselian hypothesis on $S$ is required. The empty base and rank-zero tori are allowed.

proof.text: Put $P_r=D_S(\mathbf Z^r)$ for $r\geq0$. On $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset S$, a map $A[\mathbf Z^r]\to B$ of $A$-algebras is uniquely determined by the units that are the images of the $r$ basis monomials: the image of $e_{(a_1,\ldots,a_r)}$ is $u_1^{a_1}\cdots u_r^{a_r}$. The affine adjunction therefore identifies $P_r$ with the group functor of $r$ units. The displayed Hopf operations identify its multiplication, unit and inverse with the pointwise ones. These formulas commute with changing $A$ and with restrictions; the scheme-morphism gluing lemma glues the identifications and their inverses over affine opens. Thus the torus hypothesis supplies an fppf cover $\{V_i\to S\}$ and group-scheme isomorphisms $P_{r_i}\times_SV_i\simeq T\times_SV_i$, where each $r_i$ is finite. This also verifies directly that the construction $P_r$ commutes with base change.

source.place: Tag 01I1, lemma-morphism-into-affine; explicit group-algebra computation and the fppf-local torus definition.

proof.text: For each fixed $r\geq0$ define $F_r(W)=\operatorname{Isom}_{W\text{-gp}}(P_r\times_SW,T\times_SW)$ on $S$-schemes. This is an fppf sheaf, as follows. Given compatible isomorphisms on an fppf cover $W_a\to W$, base-change that cover to $P_r\times_SW$ and to $T\times_SW$. The two resulting covers are fppf and hence fpqc. Representable fpqc descent glues the maps and their inverses uniquely. Equality of the composites with the identities, and equality of the two maps expressing preservation of multiplication, unit and inverse, can be tested on these covers and their base changes to the relevant products. Uniqueness in the same descent statement gives all those equalities over $W$. Hence the glued map is a group-scheme isomorphism. No affine or quasi-compact hypothesis on $W$ is used.

Let $E_{ri}=\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathbf Z}(\mathbf Z^{r_i},\mathbf Z^r)$, a set, and put $L_{ri}=\coprod_{e\in E_{ri}}V_i$. The chosen splitting on $V_i$ identifies $F_r|_{V_i}$ with $h_{L_{ri}}$ on ALL $V_i$-schemes. Indeed, on each nonempty affine open of a test scheme, character duality says a homomorphism between the split diagonalizable groups is uniquely locally $D(u)$ for a lattice map $u$. Applying it also to the inverse, their two composites being identities says exactly that $u$ is invertible. Thus an isomorphism gives a locally constant function to $E_{ri}$. Conversely such a function gives the maps $D(u)$ on its open-and-closed fibres; these glue uniquely, with their inverses. Maps to $\coprod_eV_i$ are precisely these labelled open-and-closed decompositions, by the coproduct's disjoint open images and universal property. This proves the asserted natural identification. Empty affine opens impose no condition; if $E_{ri}$ is empty, the represented functor has a section only on the empty test scheme.

source.place: Appendix B.1, pp.280-281, character description; agent deduction of the split-isomorphism functor using the cited character-duality statement.

proof.text: Form the scheme $U_r=\coprod_iL_{ri}$ and the natural map $q_r:h_{U_r}\to F_r$ from the local identifications. For any test scheme $Z$ and $a\in F_r(Z)$, its sheaf pullback along $q_r$ is represented by $\coprod_i(Z\times_SV_i)$: a point of the pullback is exactly a choice of covering member together with the restriction of $a$, whose image in $L_{ri}$ is unique by step 3. This formula is compatible with restrictions and with coproduct components. The projection to $Z$ is surjective, flat and locally of finite presentation, since $\{Z\times_SV_i\to Z\}$ is the base-changed fppf cover; flatness and local finite presentation are local on the disjoint open source components. Thus $q_r$ satisfies every scheme-test hypothesis of the fppf atlas bootstrap. Since $F_r$ is a sheaf by step 2, that theorem makes $F_r$ an algebraic space. All these coproducts are set-indexed in the project's size convention.

source.place: Tag 04S6, theorem-final-bootstrap, condition (3); topologies.tex Tag 021O; descent.tex Tags 04R1,04R3 for source locality.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $W_r\to F_r$. Each $L_{ri}\to V_i$ is etale: on each open component it is the identity, so the source-locality theorem applies (the empty source is allowed). Base change of the atlas identifies $W_r\times_SV_i\to L_{ri}$ with a representable etale scheme morphism. Its composite $W_r\times_SV_i\to V_i$ is therefore etale. The original fppf cover $\{V_i\to S\}$ is an fpqc cover, so fpqc descent of etaleness for SCHEME morphisms shows that $W_r\to S$ is etale. In this application the source is $W_r$, not the possibly nonschematic space $F_r$; hence no representability of $F_r\to S$ is being presumed.

source.place: Tag 02VN, lemma-descending-property-etale; morphisms.tex Tag 02GN; spaces.tex Tag 025Y for the atlas.

proof.text: The set-indexed family $\{W_r\to S\}_{r\geq0}$ is jointly surjective. For $s\in S$, choose $i$ and a point $v\in V_i$ above $s$. The chosen splitting gives a section of $F_{r_i}$ over $V_i$, so its value at $v$ gives a point of $F_{r_i}$ above $s$. Surjectivity of $W_{r_i}\to F_{r_i}$ lifts this point after a field extension, giving a point of $W_{r_i}$ above $s$. The atlas map $h_{W_r}\to F_r$, evaluated at the identity of $W_r$, is by the definition of $F_r$ a group-scheme isomorphism $P_r\times_SW_r\simeq T\times_SW_r$. Invert it and set $M_r=\mathbf Z^r$ to obtain exactly the asserted trivializations. If $S$ is empty, take the empty family. Rank zero is included: $\mathbf Z^0=0$ and its diagonalizable group is the trivial group.

The statement and its stmt_deps are unchanged, and the delivery adds no new nodes. The six steps are a correct proof that works over any base. Step 1: the affine adjunction, the Laurent/Hopf formulas and gluing turn the def-sfb-relative-torus functor isomorphisms into group-scheme splittings P_{r_i}xV_i = TxV_i. Step 2: F_r = Isom_gp(P_r, T) is an fppf sheaf by fppf base change, fppf being fpqc, and representable fpqc descent (existence and uniqueness). Step 3: character duality (A nonzero, finite free lattices) gives F_r|V_i = h_{L_ri}, with L_ri the coproduct of copies of V_i indexed by Isom(Z^{r_i},Z^r); this set is empty when the ranks differ, which is handled. Step 4: I recomputed h_Z x_F U_r as the coproduct of the Z x_S V_i. This is the base-changed fppf cover, so the fppf atlas bootstrap applies, and it matches Stacks 04S6 condition (4) in bootstrap.tex. Step 5: W_r x_S V_i equals the pullback of h_{W_r} and h_{L_ri} over F_r, which is étale over L_ri, which is étale over V_i; fpqc descent of étaleness for scheme maps then makes W_r -> S étale. Step 6: joint surjectivity comes from the splitting section and atlas surjectivity, and the tautological section gives the trivialization; the empty base and rank 0 are covered. No Noetherian or normality hypothesis is used. There is no cycle, and no duplicate: lem-sfb-normal-torus-finite-etale-splitting is only a special case.
